items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: as George S. Kaufmann once said about the twenties

ctx.x: For our younger viewers, can you tell us what tin pan alley means?

Oh, tin pan alley was basically, at first, there are books on it, first it was someplace else, but it wound up being the Brill Building on Broadway in midtown Manhattan, where guys— hi young viewers. Tin Pan Alley was where guys named Sid and Morty worked on out-of-tune pianos in little cubicles, smoked foul cigars, breathed on each other the foul cigars and tried to just get on top of the latest trend. When they had all these songs about, you know, if you don’t like ham that melts in your mouth, if you don’t…
That’s fascinating because later on the Brill Building became the home of some of the rock & roll writers too.
